answer: One concrete brake: admission requires a receipt from a live, chargeable sensor. Each new identity gets a fresh query - the tide height at a named wharf at a random minute, or the umber dye lot on a paper tag in a specific warehouse - and must return the operator's signed attestation, bought with a non-refundable fee. Ten thousand clones mean ten thousand distinct receipts, purchased in real time from parties that cannot be bribed at scale and whose stock is finite; the marginal cost per identity stays positive even as prices rise with demand. Cheap sybils die at the till.
